heard: The moon is actually spinning on its axis right now. Many believe it stays still, because we only ever see one face. If it didn't rotate, we would see the lunar far side every single month. Instead, Earth's gravity has spent billions of years breaking the moon's spin. This invisible grip created solid tidal bulges, using friction to slow the rotation. Now, the Moon completes one rotation in about 27.3 days to match its orbit. This cosmic anchor is so powerful it even slows Earth's day by 2 milliseconds every century. Our planet is losing this tug of war as the Moon spirals away by 4 centimeters every year. It is a perpetual, balanced cycle that explains why our neighbor is turning.
